compareCandidate.label: Skeletal vs. cardiac muscle
compareCandidate.description: Skeletal muscles move your body when you decide to and tire with work. Cardiac muscle is only in the heart, contracts automatically, and never tires - like a perfect engine that never stops.

plainLanguageExplanation: Muscles are tissues that can shorten (contract) to pull on bones and create movement. There are three types. Skeletal muscle attaches to bones and moves your body when you decide to move - it is striated (striped) and under your control. Smooth muscle is found in organs like the stomach and blood vessels; it works automatically. Cardiac muscle is only in the heart, beats automatically, and never tires. Skeletal muscles work in pairs: when one shortens (contracts) another relaxes, and together they move a joint. Muscles need energy and use it when they work, which is why you get tired and breathe faster during exercise.

whyItMatters: Muscles let you run, lift, breathe, digest, and pump blood. Understanding the three types and how muscles pull on bones explains why exercise makes you stronger, why the heart never stops, and how every move you make happens.
didYouKnow: You have over 600 skeletal muscles - and the strongest one, the masseter in your jaw, can bite down with more force than any other muscle for its size.
